comments.note: MovieListItem.HasCoverImage is always false until M9. The type annotation does not hint at this deferral; a developer reading only the model would not know why this field is always false. The plan documents this, but a code comment (e.g. '// always false until M9 populates cover-image filesystem discovery') directly on the property would be self-documenting. Since adding a comment to a property I did not change conflicts with the 'no docstrings on untouched code' rule, this is recorded as an observation rather than fixed.

IReadOnlyDictionary<string, bool> is the declared type for MoviesListOptions.ColumnVisibility, but the concrete type stored in the default initializer is Dictionary<string, bool>. When deserialized from JSON via Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration, the binder will replace this with a Dictionary<string, bool> anyway, so the interface type is mostly decorative. This is a minor inconsistency but not a bug.

comments.note: No Fix-Forward changes applied. Implementation is clean across all five source files.

ColumnKeys static nested class within MoviesListOptions is a strong design pattern — single source of truth for all column key strings, preventing magic-string drift between C#, AXAML bindings, and appsettings.json. The column alignment in the ColumnVisibility initializer enhances readability significantly.

IReadOnlyDictionary<string, bool> for ColumnVisibility: declared type communicates intended read-only contract to callers; concrete initializer is Dictionary<string, bool>. Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration binder creates a new Dictionary<string, bool> on binding regardless. The inconsistency is cosmetic and has been documented in prior pipelines — no action required.

MovieListQuery docstring references 'M5 will add filter and search predicates without changing the interface signature' — this is accurate milestone context and helpful for future contributors. Minor risk: if M5 does change the signature, the comment becomes misleading. Not a blocker.
